subject: Prepay refund structure and term offsets — DS Enterprise evaluation
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@datasprint.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prepay structure and early termination mechanics

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — DataSprint's eval team is broadly positive on Redwood's latency and KV cache behavior. Procurement and legal are pulling together commercial terms now. A few points we need clarity on before we can move to an LOI: 

- If we do a multi-year prepaid commitment (3x annual), what is Redwood's standard approach for refunds if we need to terminate early for convenience? Are refunds cash or credits?
- How do ramp schedules factor into refunds? We expect usage to ramp over the first 6–12 months; we want the economics to reflect that rather than a flat prepay amortization.
- Co-terming: we have other agreements with vendors that may need to co-term later in the first year — how do co-terming adjustments affect the refund math and discount amortization?

Can you share a sample refund schedule and any contract language you typically accept for early termination? Procurement would like to have a redline-ready item set.

Appreciate it — happy to set a quick call if it's easier.

Best,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Procurement, DataSprint AI
elena.torres@datasprint.ai

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@datasprint.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay structure and early termination mechanics

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, and I attached a couple artifacts for context (term calc workbook + our typical redlines):

1) Refunds: We offer two standard approaches: (A) prorated cash refund of unused prepaid value with an administrative processing fee, or (B) account credits (non-expiring for enterprise customers) convertible to Redwood services. Cash refunds require an early termination fee to cover lost committed capacity.

2) Ramp schedules: We model ramp explicitly in the TermCalc workbook by aligning the committed fiat value against expected usage months. Refunds are computed on remaining committed value less realized usage + stepwise termination charges. I included an example for a 36-month prepay with a 6-month ramp.

3) Co-terming: We can support co-term adjustments but they are treated as an alignment event — refunds/credits are computed pro rata to remaining commitment at the co-term date. Co-terming can trigger a small reconciliation fee if it reduces expected utilization density for reserved GPU pools.

Attached: RI_MultiYear_TermCalc.xlsx, Redwood_Standard_AMC_redlines_v2.pdf

If it's helpful, we can propose two commercial templates for DataSprint: (1) 3-year prepay with 15% up-front discount + prorated cash refund (administrative fee = 6% + termination fee schedule), or (2) 3-year prepay with 18% up-front discount + credits-only refund (no cash out; credits applied to future invoices).

Happy to hop on a call tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales — Large Accounts
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Prepay structure and early termination mechanics

Elena — quick note from the commercial side with a concrete optional concession you can take to procurement: 

Option A (Cash-refund path):
- 3-year prepay, 15% up-front discount
- Administrative processing fee: 6% of prepaid amount
- Early-termination schedule: months 1–12 -> 50% of remaining prepaid value refundable; months 13–24 -> 70% refundable; months 25–36 -> 85% refundable. Refunds netted against realized usage and any outstanding invoices.

Option B (Credit-only path — favoured by finance):
- 3-year prepay, 18% up-front discount
- No cash refund; remaining prepaid value converts to account credit calculated pro rata at termination date
- Credits usable across Redwood products; can be applied to dedicated or hosted routes.

We can also offer a hybrid: cash refund up to 50% of remaining balance for the first 12 months, remainder in credits.

If DataSprint needs co-term language, we recommend a joint reconciliation clause: both parties agree to a one-time cash/credit reconciliation within 60 days of co-terming event.

If you want us to accept more aggressive refund percentages, I need a quick nod from finance (copied: priyom).

—Rishi
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lee <m.lee@datasprint.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@datasprint.ai>, procurement@datasprint.ai
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: DS redlines (early termination / refund mechanics)

Lauren / Rishi — attaching our redlines (DS_Redlines_v3.docx). High level asks from legal/procurement: 

1) Termination for convenience allowed with 30 days' notice.
2) Refund (if any) must be processed within 60 days of termination and may be cash or invoice credit; preference is cash.
3) If Redwood claims a termination fee, we need a clear formula (not a discretionary admin fee).
4) Co-terming: if DataSprint elects to co-term other vendor agreements to align with Redwood, Redwood must provide a reconciliation calculation within 30 days and, if a refund is due, issue cash within 60 days.

We're okay with a step schedule but require the exact percentages/formula be included in the contract appendix. Please mark up the attached ASA with proposed percentages for review.

Marcus
Marcus Lee
Senior Counsel, DataSprint AI
m.lee@datasprint.ai

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lee <m.lee@datasprint.ai>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@datasprint.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DS redlines (early termination / refund mechanics) — proposed language

Marcus / Elena,

Thanks for the clean asks. I've taken a pass and inserted precise language and a reproducible refund formula in the appendix. Key points: 

- Termination for convenience: permitted with 30 days' notice.
- Refund formula (Appendix A): Remaining Prepaid Value * Refund Factor - Termination Fee - Administrative Fee.
  - Refund Factor table (by month of termination in a 36-month term): months 1–12 = 0.50; months 13–24 = 0.70; months 25–36 = 0.85.
  - Termination Fee: flat 3% of remaining prepaid value (covers GPU pool reallocation).
  - Administrative Fee: flat 6% of remaining prepaid value (processing + reconciliation).
- Refund currency: cash or invoice credit at Customer election. Refunds issued within 60 days of termination notice and reconciliation.
- Co-terming reconciliation: Redwood will produce a reconciliation statement within 30 days; any cash refund is payable within 60 days.

I attached a marked PDF (Redwood_Standard_AMC_redlines_v2.pdf) and an updated example worksheet showing three test cases (early termination at month 4, month 15, month 29). Example: 3-year prepay $1,200,000; termination at month 15 -> Remaining Prepaid Value $800,000 * 0.70 - 3% TermFee ($24,000) - 6% Admin ($48,000) => Refund $800,000*0.70=560,000; less 72,000 => $488,000.

If this language looks good to DataSprint legal, we can prepare an LOI with the selected discount and the appendix embedded.

Regards,
Lauren

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>

Approve: 15% cash-refund option or 18% credit-only option.
